Quote lacked the operative sentence ('is requested to be submitted in the marketing authorization applications') and the first listed situation (no previous MA in Egypt); quote and statement extended.

row.quote: The full PSMF (along together with its summary) is requested to be submitted in the marketing authorization applications (i.e. pre-authorization) in the following situations: • The applicant has not previously held a marketing authorization in Egypt, full PSMF is appropriate to review the description of a pharmacovigilance system; • The applicant has not previously submitted the PSMF in Egypt or is in the process of establishing a new pharmacovigilance system; • The applicant has major changes in its pharmacovigilance system or in its organization, such as mergers and acquisitions, where an acquisition action plan shall be provided with the PSMF (clarifying the roles and responsibility of each party during the acquisition period). • The applicant has major or critical findings in the previous pharmacovigilance system assessment by EDA;
row.statement: The applicant must submit the full PSMF together with its summary in the marketing authorisation application (pre-authorisation) where, among other listed situations, it has not previously held an MA in Egypt, has not previously submitted the PSMF in Egypt or is establishing a new PV system, has major PV system or organisational changes such as mergers and acquisitions (with an acquisition action plan clarifying each party's roles provided with the PSMF), or has major or critical findings in EDA's previous PV system assessment.

row.title: Submit the full PSMF with its summary post-authorisation when EDA requests it
row.statement: When EDA requests it post-authorisation (particularly where a new PV system is being implemented, product-specific safety concerns or PV compliance issues have been identified, in preparation for an inspection, or at any time), the MAH must submit the full PSMF together with its summary.

row.statement: When assessing seriousness of AEs/ADRs, the MAH may classify important medical events that are not immediately life-threatening and do not result in death or hospitalisation as serious where, based on medical and scientific judgement, they might jeopardise the patient or require intervention to prevent a serious outcome (e.g. emergency treatment for allergic bronchospasm, blood dyscrasias or convulsions without hospitalisation, dependency).
